C-INDEX-METRIC-2.IntentSummary:
Convert the record engine's index budget from whole-file lines to the live-`Entry` count, ship the genre-aware index breach diagnostic, regenerate the one invalidated golden file, correct the governed prose, and re-select the roots-invariant tripwire's metric — per the approved spec `.ngrace/changes/active/C-INDEX-METRIC-2/spec.xml` and only within it; the plan conforms to the spec, it does not extend, narrow or reinterpret it. DurableScope anchors exactly the one module the spec's AffectedAreas names, M-GRAMMAR (the LINKS target of src/artifact/xml.ts:5, whose parser the record engine is built on); no other anchor is named and no synthetic module is minted — none of the six governed write paths sits under src/, so the module-ownable predicate (src/lint/core.ts:724) is never satisfied and change.graph-anchors-miss-write-scope cannot fire for any anchor choice.
ObservedWriteScope is exactly the spec's six governed files — scripts/validate-record-retirement.ts, scripts/validate-record-retirement.test.ts, scripts/fixtures/record-parse/golden/decisions.xml, docs/plans/active/RM-GOVERNED-PATH/decisions.xml, CLAUDE.md and docs/plans/README.md. The bundle's own spec.xml and plan.xml are deliberately absent: the scope audit expects them outside ObservedWriteScope at plan-approve, and run-ledger.xml and run/** are tool-owned lifecycle paths no plan declares. The record root line is written once by the authority as part of this bundle's own approved diff (the M1 act the spec's second Goal defines); no task writes it and no task may claim a test guarantees the rewritten triple — the roots-invariant instrument observes exactly two relations, base equals its live-`Entry` count read back and base + headroom = ceiling, and the residual hand-edit window AC-INDEX-ROOT-REWRITTEN states stays open by design. The rewritten values are the spec's own derivation; verifying them at the record write is the authority's act. AGENTS.md is a symlink to CLAUDE.md (git mode 120000, measured at this revision) and is neither edited nor written by any task — a write through the link is either a no-op or silently un-twins the two names.
Decomposition and the red window (spec P1): four sequential tasks. T-001 lands the engine conversion at all three metric sites — the validator's index ceiling check (scripts/validate-record-retirement.ts:1423), the retire path's index persist (scripts/validate-record-retirement.ts:1244) and the split path's index base (scripts/validate-record-retirement.ts:591 and :595) — behind one exported module-level constant, plus the genre-aware diagnostic, plus the golden regeneration; its boundary is green because the standing suite's only conversion-sensitive pin is the golden (no shipped test drives an index breach — the spec's T5), the findings and rulings messages are byte-unchanged, and the roots-invariant test still compares the unchanged record against its old line metric. T-002 adds the net-new fixture tests against the already-converted engine; additive tests cannot redden a green suite. T-003 corrects CLAUDE.md and docs/plans/README.md and extends the CLAUDE/README teaching test (scripts/validate-record-retirement.test.ts:340-362) in the same task, so the extended test and the clause it requires land together and the boundary is green. T-004 re-selects the tripwire metric for decisions.xml and edits the stale line-metric comment (scripts/validate-record-retirement.test.ts:2034-2038) last, because landing it earlier would hold the suite red across every later boundary — the suite is red in the reverse partial orders (the spec's T4 measurement), which is why T-004 is last and depends on all three predecessors. Exactly one boundary is unavoidably red: after T-004 and before the authority's M1 record write, the full suite shows exactly one failure, the roots-invariant test at `decisions.xml: base equals its shipped metric read back`. That window is authority-closed and expected; the engine change, the tripwire selection and the record root rewrite land in the same commit, and the write closes the window.
Fix budgets (spec T1): FIX_SIGNATURE_REPEAT_BUDGET = 2 (src/grace-cursor.ts:187) and FIX_DISTINCT_SIGNATURE_BUDGET = 4 (src/grace-cursor.ts:193) fire per task on the same signature twice or four distinct signatures. A single task bundling engine, tests, fixture and prose would carry at least four unrelated failure surfaces (metric pair, diagnostic, split relations, golden bytes, teaching tokens) and burn the distinct budget on unrelated causes; splitting the engine from its golden would open a red window (the converted engine writes a different golden root line, so engine and regeneration are one task); splitting the prose from the teaching-test extension would open another (the extended test requires the clause). Each task below carries one failure family: T-001 the golden bytes, T-002 the new fixtures, T-003 the teaching tokens, T-004 the single expected red. That is the decomposition satisfying both budgets and the one-red-window rule together.
Golden honesty (spec T2): the one-time proof that regeneration hides nothing is an execution-time dated probe run in T-001 — the committed golden bytes pinned to this bundle's base commit (3ba0d77a76ba108be5a60e740d83dc2b734a7c46, the baseCommit recorded in this bundle's run-ledger.xml) diffed against the file this task writes, the diff shown to be exactly one line, the RecordIndex root open tag. Both sides are pinned to this bundle's own range at the moment both are alive; the probe is a dated measurement recorded in the executor's report, never a standing criterion — a close criterion comparing a fixed base commit against a floating working-tree read stops describing its own bundle the moment a later bundle touches the same bytes (staged finding F215), so no close instrument here reads a base commit: the close-time instruments are the suite and the lint, which pin the end state without one. The standing pin is the golden test itself (scripts/validate-record-retirement.test.ts:1835).
Assertion wiring (spec T3): baseline assertions pin the shipped line-metric world and go red exactly when the task that rewrites each pin lands — the four engine pins at T-001, the teaching and comment pins at T-003 and T-004, the suite MustPassCommand at T-004 (the open window). Target assertions are satisfiable at the target gate, which runs after the executor's writes and before the authority's record write: nothing in TargetAssertions depends on the record write, no target MustPassCommand runs the full suite (the roots-invariant test is red in the open window — the full suite is close-bound evidence through the spec's CloseEvidence commands, green again after the write), and the two target commands — the golden subset and the real-record validator — are green on both sides of the write. Final mode evaluates these same target assertions as the outer gate, after the record write, where they are green. No Command text anywhere below contains `--assertions current`, and none invokes a lint of this project root omitting `--assertions`: current-mode lint re-evaluates active baselines and is expected red between T-001's first write and archive (a conversion bundle's root lint is red in that window by design — the C-REPORT-HONESTY framing — so no task's completion depends on it and the only current-mode lint of this root in this bundle is the post-archive CloseEvidence of AC-CLOSE-LINT).
Execution/close boundary (spec T4): this plan covers execution only. Tasks emit the cursor events the ngrace-execute skill assigns to execution — opened (epoch open at the first task's start), progress (task start and completion), attempt (every verification cycle, with signature kind and key on fail), verification-unavailable (when evidence cannot be collected), pause and resume around interruptions, and terminal immediately before folding the quiescent epoch, then cursor fold. Tasks must not emit or perform anything belonging to the close: no gate approve, gate verdict, gate apply or gate archive; no ngrace supersede; no status write to applied; no archive move; and none of the CLI-written kinds (escalation, circuit, command-run, discarded) may be invented by hand. The spec's Constraint fixes the role split: the executor authors artifacts and reports; it does not approve, commit, push or run a gate.
No task carries a Satisfies element: every AC-* in the approved spec carries a complete CloseEvidence child, the shipped rule treats that as the third state that is not a forgotten mapping, and a Satisfies of a close-bound criterion is the error change.close-evidence-and-satisfied (src/artifact/grammar.ts:2087). Every Criterion below names the mutation that turns it red. Assertions state invariants and relations, never occupancy or archive-directory counts. Names are mandated here so the pins are satisfiable: the engine gains `export const INDEX_HEADROOM_ENTRIES = 40;` and `function liveEntryCount(xml: string): number` (the mirror of liveRowCount at scripts/validate-record-retirement.ts:975, parsing as decisions.xml and counting direct `Entry` children whose `layer` attribute is not "retired"), and the governed prose gains the exact clause tokens the extended teaching test requires. When this plan must name a tag or attribute form it writes character data with entities (`<`, `>`, `&`) and never paraphrases the brackets away. Explicit generous timeouts on every net-new test that spawns a process (F185).

T-001.Title: Convert the index metric to the live-`Entry` count at all three call sites behind one exported constant, ship the genre-aware index breach diagnostic, and regenerate the golden decisions.xml with the one-line diff shown

AcceptanceCriteria.Criterion: In scripts/validate-record-retirement.ts, add `export const INDEX_HEADROOM_ENTRIES = 40;` — one named module-level constant denominated in entries, the two headroom sites the spec's T2 names both reading it — and add `function liveEntryCount(xml: string): number`, the mirror of liveRowCount (scripts/validate-record-retirement.ts:975): parseGraceXmlArtifact over the given text as decisions.xml, then the count of direct `Entry` children of the parsed root whose `layer` attribute is not "retired". Convert all three call sites to it, each with its named red-making mutation: the validator's index ceiling check (scripts/validate-record-retirement.ts:1423, shipping `checkCeilingValue("index", paths.index, indexRoot, liveEntryCount(files.index!), "live-entry", findings)` — the registry-genre shape already shipped for live-row budgets — where the mutation is the "line" unit reverting); the retire path's index persist (scripts/validate-record-retirement.ts:1244, shipping `persistSnapshot(indexPrev, liveEntryCount(indexXml), INDEX_HEADROOM_ENTRIES, true)`); and the split path's index base (scripts/validate-record-retirement.ts:591 and :595, shipping `const indexBaseProbe = liveEntryCount(wrapRoot("RecordIndex", indexBody, {}));` with its headroom read from the constant, not a second literal). The clamp in persistSnapshot (scripts/validate-record-retirement.ts:942) is untouched: ceilings still only hold or fall. The retire path's early return is not touched either: retireRecord still early-returns when nothing is eligible (scripts/validate-record-retirement.ts:1134-1135), so the conversion gives the index genre a retirement rule that relieves it and adds no new tool mode.

The index ceiling-breach message is genre-aware, shipped in this task: for the index, the emitted flattened message reports the live-`Entry` count against the persisted ceiling and reads `live index live-entry count N exceeds persisted ceiling M; --retire / the eligible entries flip their index Entry layer to retired in place; the index has no retired sibling and its Entry lines stay. Raising the persisted ceiling is not the remedy.` — it names `--retire` as the operation, states the flip mechanic, keeps the prohibition verbatim, and its flattened text contains neither `config key` nor `ignoredDirs`. The findings, rulings and registry messages are byte-unchanged: the shared remedy line (`move the eligible entry to the retired sibling`) survives for them, as does checkCeilingValue's template shape (scripts/validate-record-retirement.ts:1498). The two clause literals live in the engine as contiguous strings so the target pins observe them.

Regenerate scripts/fixtures/record-parse/golden/decisions.xml from the converted engine's fixture `--retire` — the golden test's own flow (scripts/validate-record-retirement.test.ts:1711-1722 and :1835): build the `--c-selection-row` fixture in a temporary root via scripts/fixtures/record-parse/build-fixture.ts, run the converted engine with `--retire docs/plans/active/RM-GOVERNED-PATH`, and copy the written decisions.xml over the committed golden; the other six golden files are not written. Before regenerating, capture the committed golden bytes pinned to this bundle's base commit (3ba0d77a76ba108be5a60e740d83dc2b734a7c46, the baseCommit in this bundle's run-ledger.xml) — `git show` of that path at that commit — and after regenerating, diff the captured bytes against the regenerated file and show the diff is exactly one changed line, the RecordIndex root open tag: from the committed `<RecordIndex base="339" headroom="2" ceiling="341">` to the converted engine's `<RecordIndex base="272" headroom="40" ceiling="312">` (the fixture instance the spec's Assumptions record: 337 direct `Entry` children, 274 live, the move flipping f21 and f21-correction). Any other differing line is a stop-and-report, not a regeneration to absorb. This diff is a dated execution-time measurement recorded in the executor's report — both sides pinned to this bundle's own range, never a standing criterion, never re-read against a later tree (the staged finding F215 rule); the standing pin is the golden test itself. The fixture's `input/` snapshot and every other file under scripts/fixtures/record-parse/ stay byte-identical (spec NonGoal). Failure: any golden byte differing for a reason other than the root line turns the golden test red.

T-002.Title: Add the net-new fixture coverage: the live-`Entry` metric discriminating pair, the genre-aware diagnostic content, and the split-path relations

AcceptanceCriteria.Criterion: scripts/validate-record-retirement.test.ts gains the discriminating metric pair, net-new (the spec's T5: no shipped test drives an index breach — both shipped ceiling-exceeded tests at scripts/validate-record-retirement.test.ts:183-201 and :634-653 drive findings, and every planted index fixture carries ceiling="1000"). First direction: an index fixture whose whole-file line count exceeds its persisted ceiling while its live-`Entry` count does not — blank lines between `Entry` elements are the honest way to separate the two counts, the fixture parses clean, and the ceiling sits between the two numbers — must validate exit 0; this is the exact fixture the shipped line metric fails, so reverting either metric half to newlineCount makes this test red (the named mutation). Second direction: an index fixture whose live-`Entry` count exceeds its persisted ceiling must exit non-zero with `ceiling-exceeded`; the mutation that makes it red is a ceiling raised to pass instead of the metric changed. Both run through runValidator on isolated temporary roots with an explicit generous timeout (F185).

A net-new test drives an index breach through a fixture with a shrunken index ceiling and asserts the message content on stderr: `ceiling-exceeded`, `live index live-entry count`, `--retire`, `the eligible entries flip their index Entry layer to retired in place`, `the index has no retired sibling and its Entry lines stay`, `Raising the persisted ceiling is not the remedy`, and — lowercased — neither `config key` nor `ignoredDirs`; a second assertions block drives a findings-genre breach on its own fixture and asserts stderr still names `move the eligible entry to the retired sibling`, pinning the other genres' byte-unchanged message. Mutations named: restoring the shared remedy string for the index makes the index assertions red; adding a config-key remediation makes the prohibition assertions red; altering the findings message makes the unchanged-genre assertion red. Explicit generous timeout (F185).

A net-new test runs `--split` against a minimal pre-split dump — one finding, one h2 decision, no registry tables, the spec's Assumption shape — in a throwaway root and asserts the written index root's relations: base equals the live-`Entry` count of the written index (parseGraceXmlArtifact plus childNodes over direct `Entry` children, `layer` not "retired"), headroom equals INDEX_HEADROOM_ENTRIES imported from the engine (the test file already imports named engine exports at scripts/validate-record-retirement.test.ts:7-14), and ceiling equals base + headroom. Discriminates both ways, per the spec's measurement: the shipped line-metric engine writes a base inflated by two on the minimal dump and fails the base assertion; the converted engine passes. Mutations named: either call site reverting to a line computation or to a second literal makes this test or the golden bytes red. Explicit generous timeout (F185).

T-003.Title: Correct the governed prose in CLAUDE.md and docs/plans/README.md and extend the CLAUDE/README teaching test with the index-flip clause in the same task

AcceptanceCriteria.Criterion: CLAUDE.md and docs/plans/README.md — the only two live files carrying the retired-sibling prose (the spec's T6 corpus sweep; AGENTS.md is a symlink to CLAUDE.md with no bytes of its own and is neither edited nor written by any task) — state the index genre's actual retirement mechanic: each carries the exact clause tokens `index Entry layers flip in place` and `the index has no retired sibling`, naming that eligible index `Entry` layers flip in place and that the index has no retired sibling. Minimal edits: every token the existing teaching test requires survives (scripts/validate-record-retirement.test.ts:340-362 — decisions.md, decisions.xml, findings, decisions, registry, index, live, retired, --retire, re-derives PaidBy, never raised, resolving CodifiedIn, a resolving TaughtIn does not move it), the overturned-criterion argument stays the spec's own, and the record's other prose is untouched. Failure: the clause removed from either named file makes the extended test red.

In the same task, extend the CLAUDE/README teaching test's per-file loop (scripts/validate-record-retirement.test.ts:340-362) with `toContain("index Entry layers flip in place")` and `toContain("the index has no retired sibling")` for both files, so the prose cannot silently regress. Landing the test extension without the prose — or the prose without the extension — reddens this boundary; that is why one task carries both. Failure: the clause absent from either file turns the extended assertions red.

T-004.Title: Re-select the roots-invariant tripwire metric for decisions.xml, edit the stale line-metric comment, and record the one expected red that the authority's M1 record write closes

AcceptanceCriteria.Criterion: The production roots-invariant test (scripts/validate-record-retirement.test.ts:2015-2046) selects the shipped metric per file with the index rule added: registry keeps the live-Row rule, decisions.xml gets the live-`Entry` count — `childNodes(root, "Entry").filter((entry) => entry.attributes.layer !== "retired").length` — and findings and rulings keep newlineCount. The stale line-metric comment (scripts/validate-record-retirement.test.ts:2034-2038) is edited in the same task to say `decisions.xml joins the live-entry metric`, removing the false `for the three line-budgeted` claim. This test reads the real record, so the engine change, this metric selection and the M1 root rewrite must land in the same commit; landing this selection before T-001 would hold the suite red across every later boundary, which is why this task is last and depends on all three predecessors. Failure: the selection reverted for decisions.xml against the rewritten root makes this test red while the rest of the suite stays green.

The open boundary, stated plainly: after this task and before the authority's M1 record write, the full suite shows exactly one failure — the roots-invariant test at `decisions.xml: base equals its shipped metric read back` — because the record still carries the pre-rewrite root while the selection now reads the live-`Entry` count. The window is authority-closed and expected: the record write is the authority's act as part of this bundle's own approved diff, never a task, its values are the spec's derivation, and the write turns the roots-invariant test green (base equals its live-`Entry` count read back; base + headroom = ceiling). This criterion claims only what the instrument observes: no task asserts the rewritten triple's headroom or ceiling against any constant, no task writes the record, and the residual hand-edit window AC-INDEX-ROOT-REWRITTEN states is not closed here. Verification evidence for this task is the expected open-window state: the roots-invariant subset exits non-zero naming exactly that decisions.xml failure, the real-record validator exits 0 (the live count does not breach the persisted ceiling on either side of the write), both sibling validators exit 0, and selected target assertions with command evidence pass — any red other than the one named failure is a fail, not a window.
